0.reason: the discriminating checks are the negative assertions the review names (no PATH, no fix the command), which fail under the declared mutation as the negative-control log records

findings.text: assert MISSING_POINTER in action compares the test's own constant, supplied to the code under test in the exit record at line 121, against the action the code composes from it, so it is a round trip rather than an independent check; the discriminating assertions are the negative ones at lines 134-135, and the recorded negative control shows the test reddens, so the guard holds, but this line alone would not catch a remedy that echoed the record's fields back unchanged.

assert MISSING_POINTER not in action in the spawn arm is trivially true because the spawn fixture writes a different pointer literal (line 150), so it cannot detect the spawn arm taking the pointer branch; the live guards there are the two assertions at lines 159-160.

the fixture hand-writes launch_failure.pointer_path into exit.json, so nothing exercises the supervisor's producer and this classifier together; a rename of pointer_path in reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:2615 would leave this test and the producer's own test green while production silently lost the path.

the fragment and the manifest state that ruff check and ruff format --check are clean on the staged paths, but no ruff log is named in the manifest's test_logs, so that half of the done_when's gate is claimed rather than recorded.
